main_body: Large leafy oak canopy (several overlapping leaf clumps) on a short, thick trunk with spreading roots
top_band: Light-green leaf clumps (#93c144, L~164) at rows 1-5 on the crown, shading down to mid and dark greens. No hard rectangular top band; the canopy's lit upper surface reads as the top.
evidence: This is an organic tree, not a box-like object. The canopy is lit from above: light clumps sit on top of each mass, with dark green shadow under each clump and a dark underside where the canopy meets the trunk. It reads as a volume seen from the south-above, like the two Beodeul reference trees. The trunk and roots flare out below the canopy. No receding side face is drawn and it is not a flat elevation. A straight-edged top and front-edge line do not apply to foliage; the tiered leaf clumps with shadow beneath them stand in for the eave shadow.

style.evidence: The canopy uses about 6 distinct greens (deep #12431d, dark #164e21, mid #297928, light #4c9036, bright #7cb23f, highlight #93c144) in clustered leaf clumps. The trunk has several brown tones with highlights. The outline is a dark green or dark brown that leans toward the neighbouring material, and only 1% of dark edge pixels are neutral. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. The measured figures match or beat the references: 109 colours per tile against 108 and 109, and 554 distinct colours against 427 and 567. Next to the references it looks equally rich, not thinner or sticker-like.
